verses.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לוֹ֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מֶרְכָּבָ֖ה וְסֻסִ֑ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî mê·’a·ḥă·rê ḵên way·ya·‘aś lōw ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm mer·kā·ḇāh wə·su·sîm wa·ḥă·miš·šîm ’îš rā·ṣîm lə·p̄ā·nāw
verses.literal: Some time later . . . . . . Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him
verses.literalPt: E ACONTECEU depois disto que Absalão fez aparelhar carros e cavalos, e cinqüenta homens que corressem adiante dele.

verses.original: וְהִשְׁכִּים֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם וְעָמַ֕ד עַל־ יַ֖ד דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיְהִ֡י כָּל־ הָאִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִהְיֶה־ לּוֹ־ רִיב֩ לָב֨וֹא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְשָׁל֤וֹם אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵֽי־ מִזֶּ֥ה עִיר֙ אַ֔תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מֵאַחַ֥ד שִׁבְטֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hiš·kîm ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm wə·‘ā·maḏ ‘al- yaḏ de·reḵ haš·šā·‘ar way·hî kāl- hā·’îš ’ă·šer- yih·yeh- lōw- rîḇ lā·ḇō·w ’el- ham·me·leḵ lam·miš·pāṭ way·yiq·rā ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’ê·lāw way·yō·mer ’ê- miz·zeh ‘îr ’at·tāh way·yō·mer mê·’a·ḥaḏ šiḇ·ṭê- yiś·rā·’êl ‘aḇ·de·ḵā
verses.literal: He would get up early and stand beside . . . the road leading to the city gate Whenever anyone . . . had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision Absalom would call out and ask What . . . city are you from And if he replied Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel
verses.literalPt: Também Absalão se levantou pela manhã, e parava a um lado do caminho da porta. E sucedia que a todo o homem que tinha alguma demanda para vir ao rei a juízo, o chamava Absalão a si, e lhe dizia: De que cidade és tu? E, dizendo ele: De uma das tribos de Israel é teu servo;

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם רְאֵ֥ה דְבָרֶ֖ךָ טוֹבִ֣ים וּנְכֹחִ֑ים וְשֹׁמֵ֥עַ אֵין־ לְךָ֖ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ê·lāw ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm rə·’êh ḏə·ḇā·re·ḵā ṭō·w·ḇîm ū·nə·ḵō·ḥîm wə·šō·mê·a‘ ’ên- lə·ḵā mê·’êṯ ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: Absalom would say . . . Look your claims are good and right but the king has no deputy to hear you
verses.literalPt: Então Absalão lhe dizia: Olha, os teus negócios são bons e retos, porém não tens quem te ouça da parte do rei.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִי־ יְשִׂמֵ֥נִי שֹׁפֵ֖ט בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְעָלַ֗י יָב֥וֹא כָּל־ אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִהְיֶה־ לּוֹ־ רִ֥יב וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וְהִצְדַּקְתִּֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm mî- yə·śi·mê·nî šō·p̄êṭ bā·’ā·reṣ wə·‘ā·lay yā·ḇō·w kāl- ’îš ’ă·šer- yih·yeh- lōw- rîḇ ū·miš·pāṭ wə·hiṣ·daq·tîw
verses.literal: And he would add If only someone would appoint me judge in the land then everyone . . . with a grievance or dispute could come to me and I would give him justice
verses.literalPt: Dizia mais Absalão: Ah, quem me dera ser juiz na terra, para que viesse a mim todo o homem que tivesse demanda ou questão, para que lhe fizesse justiça!

verses.original: וְהָיָה֙ בִּקְרָב־ אִ֔ישׁ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת ל֑וֹ וְשָׁלַ֧ח אֶת־ יָד֛וֹ וְהֶחֱזִ֥יק ל֖וֹ וְנָ֥שַׁק לֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hā·yāh biq·rāḇ- ’îš lə·hiš·ta·ḥă·wōṯ lōw wə·šā·laḥ ’eṯ- yā·ḏōw wə·he·ḥĕ·zîq lōw wə·nā·šaq lōw
verses.literal: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him Absalom would reach out his hand take hold of him and kiss him
verses.literalPt: Sucedia também que, quando alguém se chegava a ele para se inclinar diante dele, ele estendia a sua mão, e pegava dele, e o beijava.

verses.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ יָבֹ֥אוּ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְגַנֵּב֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אֶת־ לֵ֖ב אַנְשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘aś ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm kad·dā·ḇār haz·zeh lə·ḵāl yiś·rā·’êl ’ă·šer- yā·ḇō·’ū lam·miš·pāṭ ’el- ham·me·leḵ way·ḡan·nêḇ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’eṯ- lêḇ ’an·šê yiś·rā·’êl
verses.literal: Absalom . . . did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel
verses.literalPt: E desta maneira fazia Absalão a todo o Israel que vinha ao rei para juízo; assim furtava Absalão o coração dos homens de Israel.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֛ם אֶת־ נִדְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ נָדַ֥רְתִּי לַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî miq·qêṣ ’ar·bā·‘îm šā·nāh way·yō·mer ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’el- ham·me·leḵ ’ê·lă·ḵāh nā wa·’ă·šal·lêm ’eṯ- niḏ·rî ’ă·šer- nā·ḏar·tî Yah·weh bə·ḥeḇ·rō·wn
verses.literal: After four years had passed Absalom said to the king Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD
verses.literalPt: Aconteceu, pois, ao cabo de quarenta anos, que Absalão disse ao rei: Deixa-me ir pagar em Hebrom o meu voto que fiz ao SENHOR.

verses.original: כִּי־ נֵ֙דֶר֙ נָדַ֣ר עַבְדְּךָ֔ בְּשִׁבְתִּ֥י בִגְשׁ֛וּר בַּאֲרָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־ יָשִׁיב יְשִׁיבֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְעָבַדְתִּ֖י אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: kî- nê·ḏer nā·ḏar ‘aḇ·də·ḵā bə·šiḇ·tî ḇiḡ·šūr ba·’ă·rām lê·mōr ’im- yå̄·šīḇ yə·šî·ḇê·nî Yah·weh yə·rū·šā·lim wə·‘ā·ḇaḏ·tî ’eṯ- Yah·weh
verses.literal: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram saying If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem I will worship the LORD in Hebron
verses.literalPt: Porque, morando eu em Gesur, na Síria, fez o teu servo um voto, dizendo: Se o SENHOR outra vez me fizer tornar a Jerusalém, servirei ao SENHOR.

verses.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵ֣ךְ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ חֶבְרֽוֹנָה׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer- lōw ham·me·leḵ lêḵ bə·šā·lō·wm way·yā·qām way·yê·leḵ ḥeḇ·rō·w·nāh
verses.literal: Go in peace said the king So Absalom got up and went to Hebron
verses.literalPt: Então lhe disse o rei: Vai em paz. Levantou-se, pois, e foi para Hebrom.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ מְרַגְּלִ֔ים בְּכָל־ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּשָׁמְעֲכֶם֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מָלַ֥ךְ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·laḥ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm mə·rag·gə·lîm bə·ḵāl šiḇ·ṭê yiś·rā·’êl lê·mōr kə·šā·mə·‘ă·ḵem ’eṯ- qō·wl haš·šō·p̄ār wa·’ă·mar·tem mā·laḵ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm bə·ḥeḇ·rō·wn
verses.literal: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message When you hear the sound of the horn you are to say Absalom reigns in Hebron
verses.literalPt: E enviou Absalão espias por todas as tribos de Israel, dizendo: Quando ouvirdes o som das trombetas, direis: Absalão reina em Hebrom.

verses.original: וְאֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם הָלְכ֞וּ מָאתַ֤יִם אִישׁ֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קְרֻאִ֖ים וְהֹלְכִ֣ים לְתֻמָּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כָּל־ דָּבָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm hā·lə·ḵū mā·ṯa·yim ’îš mî·rū·šā·lim qə·ru·’îm wə·hō·lə·ḵîm lə·ṯum·mām wə·lō yā·ḏə·‘ū kāl- dā·ḇār
verses.literal: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied . . . Absalom They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently for they knew nothing about the matter
verses.literalPt: E de Jerusalém foram com Absalão duzentos homens convidados, porém iam na sua simplicidade, porque nada sabiam daquele negócio.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אַ֠בְשָׁלוֹם אֶת־ אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל הַגִּֽילֹנִ֜י יוֹעֵ֣ץ דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִגִּלֹ֔ה בְּזָבְח֖וֹ אֶת־ הַזְּבָחִ֑ים וַיְהִ֤י הַקֶּ֙שֶׁר֙ אַמִּ֔ץ וְהָעָ֛ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וָרָ֖ב אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·laḥ ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ’eṯ- ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el hag·gî·lō·nî yō·w·‘êṣ dā·wiḏ mê·‘î·rōw mig·gi·lōh bə·zā·ḇə·ḥōw ’eṯ- haz·zə·ḇā·ḥîm way·hî haq·qe·šer ’am·miṣ wə·hā·‘ām hō·w·lêḵ wā·rāḇ ’eṯ- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite David’s counselor to come from his hometown of Giloh So the conspiracy gained strength and Absalom’s following kept increasing . . .
verses.literalPt: Também Absalão mandou vir Aitofel, o gilonita, do conselho de Davi, à sua cidade de Giló, estando ele oferecendo os seus sacrifícios; e a conjuração se fortificava, e vinha o povo, e ia crescendo com Absalão.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּגִּ֔יד אֶל־ דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הָיָ֛ה לֶב־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ham·mag·gîḏ ’el- dā·wiḏ lê·mōr hā·yāh leḇ- ’îš yiś·rā·’êl ’a·ḥă·rê ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm
verses.literal: Then a messenger came to David and reported The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom
verses.literalPt: Então veio um mensageiro a Davi, dizendo: O coração de cada um em Israel segue a Absalão.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּ֠וִד לְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֨יו אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֤וֹ בִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ ק֣וּמוּ וְנִבְרָ֔חָה כִּ֛י לֹא־ תִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥נוּ פְלֵיטָ֖ה מִפְּנֵ֣י אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם מַהֲר֣וּ לָלֶ֗כֶת פֶּן־ יְמַהֵ֤ר וְהִשִּׂגָ֙נוּ֙ וְהִדִּ֤יחַ עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וְהִכָּ֥ה הָעִ֖יר לְפִי־ חָֽרֶב׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ lə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw ḇî·rū·šā·lim qū·mū wə·niḇ·rā·ḥāh kî lō- ṯih·yeh- lā·nū p̄ə·lê·ṭāh mip·pə·nê ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ma·hă·rū lā·le·ḵeṯ pen- yə·ma·hêr wə·hiś·śi·ḡā·nū wə·hid·dî·aḥ ‘ā·lê·nū ’eṯ- hā·rā·‘āh wə·hik·kāh hā·‘îr lə·p̄î- ḥā·reḇ
verses.literal: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem Arise and let us flee or we will not escape from Absalom We must leave quickly or he will soon overtake us heap disaster on us and put the city to the sword
verses.literalPt: Disse, pois, Davi a todos os seus servos que estavam com ele em Jerusalém: Levantai-vos, e fujamos, porque não poderíamos escapar diante de Absalão. Dai-vos pressa a caminhar, para que porventura não se apresse ele, e nos alcance, e lance sobre nós algum mal, e fira a cidade a fio de espada.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֛ר אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū ‘aḇ·ḏê- ham·me·leḵ ’el- ham·me·leḵ kə·ḵōl ’ă·šer- yiḇ·ḥar ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ hin·nêh ‘ă·ḇā·ḏe·ḵā
verses.literal: The king’s servants replied - Whatever our lord the king . . . decides we are your servants
verses.literalPt: Então os servos do rei disseram ao rei: Eis aqui os teus servos, para tudo quanto determinar o rei, nosso senhor.

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ בֵּית֖וֹ בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֵ֣ת עֶ֧שֶׂר נָשִׁ֛ים פִּֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֥ר הַבָּֽיִת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣê ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵāl bê·ṯōw bə·raḡ·lāw way·ya·‘ă·zōḇ ham·me·leḵ ’êṯ ‘e·śer nā·šîm pi·laḡ·šîm liš·mōr hab·bā·yiṯ
verses.literal: Then the king set out and his entire household followed him But he left behind ten . . . concubines to take care of the palace
verses.literalPt: E saiu o rei, com toda a sua casa, a pé; deixou, porém, o rei dez mulheres concubinas, para guardarem a casa.

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּרְחָֽק׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣê ham·me·leḵ wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām bə·raḡ·lāw way·ya·‘am·ḏū bêṯ ham·mer·ḥāq
verses.literal: So the king set out with all the people following him He stopped at the last house
verses.literalPt: Tendo, pois, saído o rei com todo o povo a pé, pararam num lugar distante.

verses.original: וְכָל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ עֹבְרִ֣ים עַל־ יָד֔וֹ וְכָל־ הַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְכָל־ הַפְּלֵתִ֑י וְכָֽל־ הַגִּתִּ֞ים שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֤אוּ בְרַגְלוֹ֙ מִגַּ֔ת עֹבְרִ֖ים עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw ‘ō·ḇə·rîm ‘al- yā·ḏōw wə·ḵāl hak·kə·rê·ṯî wə·ḵāl hap·pə·lê·ṯî wə·ḵāl hag·git·tîm šêš- mê·’ō·wṯ ’îš ’ă·šer- bā·’ū ḇə·raḡ·lōw mig·gaṯ ‘ō·ḇə·rîm ‘al- pə·nê ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: and all his servants marched past him all the Cherethites and Pelethites and six hundred Gittites . . . who had followed him from Gath -
verses.literalPt: E todos os seus servos iam a seu lado, como também todos os quereteus e todos os peleteus; e todos os giteus, seiscentos homens que vieram de Gate a pé, caminhavam diante do rei.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֔י לָ֧מָּה תֵלֵ֛ךְ גַּם־ אַתָּ֖ה אִתָּ֑נוּ שׁ֣וּב וְשֵׁ֤ב עִם־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ כִּֽי־ נָכְרִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וְגַם־ גֹּלֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה לִמְקוֹמֶֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- ’it·tay hag·git·tî lām·māh ṯê·lêḵ gam- ’at·tāh ’it·tā·nū šūḇ wə·šêḇ ‘im- ham·me·leḵ kî- nā·ḵə·rî ’at·tāh wə·ḡam- gō·leh ’at·tāh lim·qō·w·me·ḵā
verses.literal: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite Why should you also go with us Go back and stay with the new king since you are both a foreigner and an exile . . . from your homeland
verses.literalPt: Disse, pois, o rei a Itai, o giteu: Por que irias tu também conosco? Volta-te, e fica-te com o rei, porque és estrangeiro, e também desterrado de teu lugar.

verses.original: תְּמ֣וֹל׀ בּוֹאֶ֗ךָ וְהַיּ֞וֹם אֲנוֹעֲךָ עִמָּ֙נוּ֙ לָלֶ֔כֶת וַאֲנִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ אֲנִ֖י הוֹלֵ֑ךְ שׁ֣וּב וְהָשֵׁ֧ב אֶת־ אַחֶ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
verses.transliteration: tə·mō·wl bō·w·’e·ḵā wə·hay·yō·wm ʾă·nō·ʿă·ḵå̄ ‘im·mā·nū lā·le·ḵeṯ wa·’ă·nî hō·w·lêḵ ‘al ’ă·šer- ’ă·nî hō·w·lêḵ šūḇ wə·hā·šêḇ ’eṯ- ’a·ḥe·ḵā ‘im·māḵ ḥe·seḏ we·’ĕ·meṯ
verses.literal: In fact, you arrived only yesterday should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going Go back and take your brothers with you May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness
verses.literalPt: Ontem vieste, e te levaria eu hoje conosco a caminhar? Pois eu vou para onde puder ir; volta, pois, e torna a levar teus irmãos contigo, com beneficência e fidelidade.

verses.original: וַיַּ֧עַן אִתַּ֛י אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חַי־ יְהוָ֗ה וְחֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֠י אִם־ בִּמְק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽהְיֶה־ שָּׁ֣ם׀ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אִם־ לְמָ֙וֶת֙ אִם־ לְחַיִּ֔ים כִּי־ שָׁ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an ’it·tay ’eṯ- ham·me·leḵ way·yō·mar ḥay- Yah·weh wə·ḥê ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ kî ’im- bim·qō·wm ’ă·šer yih·yeh- šām ’ă·ḏō·nî ham·me·leḵ ’im- lə·mā·weṯ ’im- lə·ḥay·yîm kî- šām yih·yeh ‘aḇ·de·ḵā
verses.literal: But Ittai answered the king As surely as the LORD lives and as my lord the king . . . lives wherever my lord the king may be whether it means life . . . . . . or death there will your servant be
verses.literalPt: Respondeu, porém, Itai ao rei, e disse: Vive o SENHOR, e vive o rei meu senhor, que no lugar em que estiver o rei meu senhor, seja para morte seja para vida, aí certamente estará também o teu servidor.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־ אִתַּ֖י לֵ֣ךְ וַעֲבֹ֑ר וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֞ר אִתַּ֤י הַגִּתִּי֙ וְכָל־ אֲנָשָׁ֔יו וְכָל־ הַטַּ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ ’el- ’it·tay lêḵ wa·‘ă·ḇōr way·ya·‘ă·ḇōr ’it·tay hag·git·tî wə·ḵāl ’ă·nā·šāw wə·ḵāl haṭ·ṭap̄ ’ă·šer ’it·tōw
verses.literal: March on then said David to Ittai . . . So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him
verses.literalPt: Então Davi disse a Itai: Vem, pois, e passa adiante. Assim passou Itai, o giteu, e todos os seus homens, e todas as crianças que havia com ele.

verses.original: וְכָל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ בּוֹכִים֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם עֹֽבְרִ֑ים וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹבֵר֙ בְּנַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ עֹבְרִ֔ים עַל־ פְּנֵי־ דֶ֖רֶךְ אֶת־ הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḵāl hā·’ā·reṣ bō·w·ḵîm qō·wl gā·ḏō·wl wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ‘ō·ḇə·rîm wə·ham·me·leḵ ‘ō·ḇêr bə·na·ḥal qiḏ·rō·wn wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ‘ō·ḇə·rîm ‘al- pə·nê- ḏe·reḵ ’eṯ- ham·miḏ·bār
verses.literal: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly . . . as all the people passed by And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness
verses.literalPt: E toda a terra chorava a grandes vozes, passando todo o povo; também o rei passou o ribeiro de Cedrom, e passou todo o povo na direção do caminho do deserto.

verses.original: וְהִנֵּ֨ה גַם־ צָד֜וֹק וְכָֽל־ הַלְוִיִּ֣ם אִתּ֗וֹ נֹֽשְׂאִים֙ אֶת־ אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֙קוּ֙ אֶת־ אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּ֖עַל אֶבְיָתָ֑ר עַד־ תֹּ֥ם כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם לַעֲב֥וֹר מִן־ הָעִֽיר׃
verses.transliteration: wə·hin·nêh ḡam- ṣā·ḏō·wq wə·ḵāl hal·wî·yim ’it·tōw nō·śə·’îm ’eṯ- ’ă·rō·wn bə·rîṯ hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm way·yaṣ·ṣi·qū ’eṯ- ’ă·rō·wn hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm way·ya·‘al ’eḇ·yā·ṯār ‘aḏ- tōm kāl- hā·‘ām la·‘ă·ḇō·wr min- hā·‘îr
verses.literal: Zadok was also there and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God And they set down the ark of God and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had passed . . . out of the city
verses.literalPt: Eis que também Zadoque ali estava, e com ele todos os levitas que levavam a arca da aliança de Deus; e puseram ali a arca de Deus, e subiu Abiatar, até que todo o povo acabou de passar da cidade.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְצָד֔וֹק הָשֵׁ֛ב אֶת־ אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הָעִ֑יר אִם־ אֶמְצָ֥א חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֶהֱשִׁבַ֕נִי וְהִרְאַ֥נִי אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־ נָוֵֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ lə·ṣā·ḏō·wq hā·šêḇ ’eṯ- ’ă·rō·wn hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm hā·‘îr ’im- ’em·ṣā ḥên bə·‘ê·nê Yah·weh we·hĕ·ši·ḇa·nî wə·hir·’a·nî ’ō·ṯōw wə·’eṯ- nā·wê·hū
verses.literal: Then the king said to Zadok Return the ark of God to the city If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again
verses.literalPt: Então disse o rei a Zadoque: Torna a levar a arca de Deus à cidade; que, se achar graça nos olhos do SENHOR, ele me tornará a trazer para lá e me deixará ver a ela e a sua habitação.

verses.original: וְאִם֙ כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֔ר לֹ֥א חָפַ֖צְתִּי בָּ֑ךְ הִנְנִ֕י יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר ט֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·’im kōh yō·mar lō ḥā·p̄aṣ·tî bāḵ hin·nî ya·‘ă·śeh- lî ka·’ă·šer ṭō·wḇ bə·‘ê·nāw
verses.literal: But if . . . He should say I do not delight in you then here I am let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him
verses.literalPt: Se, porém, disser assim: Não tenho prazer em ti; eis-me aqui, faça de mim como parecer bem aos seus olhos.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֔ן הֲרוֹאֶ֣ה אַתָּ֔ה שֻׁ֥בָה הָעִ֖יר בְּשָׁל֑וֹם וַאֲחִימַ֨עַץ בִּנְךָ֜ וִיהוֹנָתָ֧ן בֶּן־ אֶבְיָתָ֛ר שְׁנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’el- ṣā·ḏō·wq hak·kō·hên hă·rō·w·’eh ’at·tāh šu·ḇāh hā·‘îr bə·šā·lō·wm wa·’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ bin·ḵā wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān ben- ’eḇ·yā·ṯār šə·nê ḇə·nê·ḵem ’it·tə·ḵem
verses.literal: The king also said to Zadok the priest Are you not a seer . . . Return to the city in peace you with your son Ahimaaz and Abiathar with his son Jonathan -
verses.literalPt: Disse mais o rei a Zadoque, o sacerdote: Não és tu porventura vidente? Torna, pois, em paz para a cidade, e convosco também vossos dois filhos, Aimás, teu filho, e Jônatas, filho de Abiatar.

verses.original: רְאוּ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י מִתְמַהְמֵ֔הַּ בְּעַבְרוֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַ֣ד בּ֥וֹא דָבָ֛ר מֵעִמָּכֶ֖ם לְהַגִּ֥יד לִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: rə·’ū ’ā·nō·ḵî miṯ·mah·mê·ah bə·ʿaḇ·rōṯ ham·miḏ·bār ‘aḏ bō·w ḏā·ḇār mê·‘im·mā·ḵem lə·hag·gîḏ lî
verses.literal: See I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me
verses.literalPt: Olhai que me demorarei nas campinas do deserto até que tenha notícias vossas.

verses.original: וַיָּ֨שֶׁב צָד֧וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֛ר אֶת־ אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·šeḇ ṣā·ḏō·wq wə·’eḇ·yā·ṯār ’eṯ- ’ă·rō·wn hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm yə·rū·šā·lim way·yê·šə·ḇū šām
verses.literal: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there
verses.literalPt: Zadoque, pois, e Abiatar, tornaram a levar para Jerusalém a arca de Deus; e ficaram ali.

verses.original: וְדָוִ֡ד עֹלֶה֩ בְמַעֲלֵ֨ה הַזֵּיתִ֜ים עֹלֶ֣ה׀ וּבוֹכֶ֗ה וְרֹ֥אשׁ לוֹ֙ חָפ֔וּי וְה֖וּא הֹלֵ֣ךְ יָחֵ֑ף וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֗וֹ חָפוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְעָל֥וּ עָלֹ֖ה וּבָכֹֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḏā·wiḏ ‘ō·leh ḇə·ma·‘ă·lêh haz·zê·ṯîm ‘ō·leh ū·ḇō·w·ḵeh wə·rōš lōw ḥā·p̄ui wə·hū hō·lêḵ yā·ḥêp̄ wə·ḵāl hā·‘ām ’ă·šer- ’it·tōw ḥā·p̄ū ’îš rō·šōw wə·‘ā·lū ‘ā·lōh ū·ḇā·ḵōh
verses.literal: But David continued up . . . the Mount of Olives weeping as he went up His head was covered and he was walking barefoot And all the people with him covered . . . their heads and went up weeping as they went
verses.literalPt: E seguiu Davi pela encosta do monte das Oliveiras, subindo e chorando, e com a cabeça coberta; e caminhava com os pés descalços; e todo o povo que ia com ele cobria cada um a sua cabeça, e subiam chorando sem cessar.

verses.original: וְדָוִד֙ הִגִּ֣יד לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲחִיתֹ֥פֶל בַּקֹּשְׁרִ֖ים עִם־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד סַכֶּל־ נָ֛א אֶת־ עֲצַ֥ת אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḏā·wiḏ hig·gîḏ lê·mōr ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el baq·qō·šə·rîm ‘im- ’aḇ·šā·lō·wm way·yō·mer dā·wiḏ sak·kel- nā ’eṯ- ‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el Yah·weh
verses.literal: Now someone told David Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom So David pleaded O LORD please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness
verses.literalPt: Então fizeram saber a Davi, dizendo: Também Aitofel está entre os que se conjuraram com Absalão. Pelo que disse Davi: Ó SENHOR, peço-te que torne em loucura o conselho de Aitofel.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֤י דָוִד֙ בָּ֣א עַד־ הָרֹ֔אשׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים וְהִנֵּ֤ה לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י קָר֙וּעַ֙ כֻּתָּנְתּ֔וֹ וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ḏā·wiḏ bā ‘aḏ- hā·rōš ’ă·šer- yiš·ta·ḥă·weh šām lê·lō·hîm wə·hin·nêh liq·rā·ṯōw ḥū·šay hā·’ar·kî qā·rū·a‘ kut·tā·nə·tōw wa·’ă·ḏā·māh ‘al- rō·šōw
verses.literal: When David came to the summit where he used to worship . . . God Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, chegando Davi ao cume, para adorar ali a Deus, eis que Husai, o arquita, veio encontrar-se com ele com a roupa rasgada e terra sobre a cabeça.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑ד אִ֚ם עָבַ֣רְתָּ אִתִּ֔י וְהָיִ֥תָ עָלַ֖י לְמַשָּֽׂא׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw dā·wiḏ ’im ‘ā·ḇar·tā ’it·tî wə·hā·yi·ṯā ‘ā·lay lə·maś·śā
verses.literal: David said to him If you go on with me you will be a burden to me
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe Davi: Se passares comigo, ser-me-ás pesado.

verses.original: וְאִם־ הָעִ֣יר תָּשׁ֗וּב וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ עַבְדְּךָ֨ אֲנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶֽהְיֶ֔ה עֶ֣בֶד אָבִ֤יךָ וַֽאֲנִי֙ מֵאָ֔ז וְעַתָּ֖ה וַאֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְהֵפַרְתָּ֣ה לִ֔י אֵ֖ת עֲצַ֥ת אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’im- hā·‘îr tā·šūḇ wə·’ā·mar·tā lə·’aḇ·šā·lō·wm ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’ă·nî ham·me·leḵ ’eh·yeh ‘e·ḇeḏ ’ā·ḇî·ḵā wa·’ă·nî mê·’āz wə·‘at·tāh wa·’ă·nî ‘aḇ·de·ḵā wə·hê·p̄ar·tāh lî ’êṯ ‘ă·ṣaṯ ’ă·ḥî·ṯō·p̄el
verses.literal: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom I will be your servant my king in the past I was your father’s servant but now I will be your servant
verses.literalPt: Porém se voltares para a cidade, e disseres a Absalão: Eu serei, ó rei, teu servo; bem fui antes servo de teu pai, mas agora serei teu servo; dissipar-me-ás então o conselho de Aitofel.

verses.original: וַהֲל֤וֹא עִמְּךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם צָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּהֲנִ֑ים וְהָיָ֗ה כָּל־ הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּשְׁמַע֙ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תַּגִּ֕יד לְצָד֥וֹק וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: wa·hă·lō·w ‘im·mə·ḵā šām ṣā·ḏō·wq wə·’eḇ·yā·ṯār hak·kō·hă·nîm wə·hā·yāh kāl- had·dā·ḇār ’ă·šer tiš·ma‘ mib·bêṯ ham·me·leḵ tag·gîḏ lə·ṣā·ḏō·wq ū·lə·’eḇ·yā·ṯār hak·kō·hă·nîm
verses.literal: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests . . . be there with you Report to them . . . . . . everything . . . you hear from the king’s palace
verses.literalPt: E não estão ali contigo Zadoque e Abiatar, sacerdotes? E será que todas as coisas que ouvires da casa do rei, farás saber a Zadoque, e a Abiatar, sacerdotes.

verses.original: הִנֵּה־ שָׁ֤ם עִמָּם֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵיהֶ֔ם אֲחִימַ֣עַץ לְצָד֔וֹק וִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן לְאֶבְיָתָ֑ר וּשְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם בְּיָדָם֙ אֵלַ֔י כָּל־ דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ׃
verses.transliteration: hin·nêh- šām ‘im·mām šə·nê ḇə·nê·hem ’ă·ḥî·ma·‘aṣ lə·ṣā·ḏō·wq wî·hō·w·nā·ṯān lə·’eḇ·yā·ṯār ū·šə·laḥ·tem bə·yā·ḏām ’ê·lay kāl- dā·ḇār ’ă·šer tiš·mā·‘ū
verses.literal: Indeed their two sons Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar are there with them Send them to me with everything . . . you hear
verses.literalPt: Eis que estão também ali com eles seus dois filhos, Aimaás filho de Zadoque, e Jônatas filho de Abiatar; pela mão deles aviso me mandareis, de todas as coisas que ouvirdes.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א חוּשַׁ֛י רֵעֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד הָעִ֑יר וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם יָבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ḥū·šay rê·‘eh ḏā·wiḏ hā·‘îr wə·’aḇ·šā·lōm yā·ḇō yə·rū·šā·lim
verses.literal: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city
verses.literalPt: Husai, pois, amigo de Davi, veio para a cidade; e Absalão entrou em Jerusalém.
